messages:
incident-bot: [PAGE] Persistent p95 latency spike observed in inference-us-west bridge pool (p95 ~ 6.2s). Error budget creeping, auto-escalate to on-call and SRE.

sre_maya: I see the spike across bridge-1 and bridge-4, tail tokens queueing and an uptick in 5xx for long-context endpoints. No node CPU or GPU memory pressure flagged. Suspect recent kernel-level batching change.

oncall_ashwin: Joining. Which commit/flag landed just before the spike?

eng_lee: Deploy at 03:05 UTC enabled `dynamic_batcher:v2` via feature flag `enable_dynamic_batcher=true` in svc-config. Canary looked ok on short-context tests but didn't exercise long-context paths.

sre_maya: Can confirm canary traffic was low for long-context tests. Suggest immediate toggle off for all bridges, plus a temporary routing diversion to healthy dedicated-us-east.

oncall_ashwin: Agreed. eng_lee, what's the fastest safe rollback?

eng_lee: Two options: 1) set feature flag to false (fast) or 2) roll back deployment to previous revision (safer for config drift). Quick command for flag toggle:
```
kubectl set env deploy/runtime ENABLE_DYNAMIC_BATCHER=false -n inference
```
This propagates within ~45-75s per pod.

platform_nina: I'll prepare a routing policy: move 25% of traffic to dedicated-us-east and set a short KV TTL to 60s to reduce long prefix retention. Doing routing change in 90s.

comms_sam: Draft status page blurb (short):
"We are investigating increased latency in US-West inference. We have disabled a recently enabled batching optimization and are routing a portion of traffic to a healthy fallback region. No customer data was impacted. We'll update every 20 minutes while we monitor."

incident-bot: action: env toggle applied to deployment/runtime; rollout initiated (rc=1). Health checks will report as pods restart.

sre_maya: Metrics: queue depth dropping ~50% on bridge-1 within 2m of flag toggle; p50 recovered to baseline, p95 down from 6.2s to 3.1s but still elevated. Error rate falling.

incident-bot: routing change executed; 25% weight shifted to dedicated-us-east. Watch for model-variant incompatibilities.

oncall_ashwin: Good. product_julia, can you coordinate customer comms for impacted tenants with account execs? Prioritize enterprise orgs with SLAs.

product_julia: On it. I'll send the short blurb to AE rotation and include an escalation contact.

eng_lee: Noted a secondary signal: KV eviction bursts when traffic reroutes back cause transient cache misses. Recommend TTL reduction and staged traffic ramp back when stable for 15m.

platform_nina: TTL set to 60s. I'll prepare a staged ramp plan: after 20m stable, shift 25% back every 5 minutes.

comms_sam: Posted status page update and emailed top 12 customers identified by SLO-populated list. Included contact for 1:1 if they see impact.

sre_maya: Please keep running the runbook checklist (link: runbooks/bridge_latency.md) — we're on step 3/6.

oncall_ashwin: Handoff plan: I'll own monitoring and cadence. If stable for 20m with p95 < 2.5s and error rate normal, we'll start the staged revert. If we see regression, escalate to platform and pause any feature flags.

eng_lee: Creating INF-8842: regression eval + canary gating for dynamic_batcher. Will attach perf tests and long-context workloads.

comms_sam: Next status update in 20 minutes. Template for internal update: "Incident: US-West inference p95 spike. Impact: increased latencies and sporadic 5xx for long-context calls. Mitigation: disabled dynamic batching, diverted traffic to fallback region, reduced KV TTL. Current status: improving, monitoring. Owner: oncall_ashwin. ETA: ongoing — updates every 20m."

incident-bot: note: pager acknowledged by oncall_ashwin at 4301012355.

oncall_ashwin: Taking over active monitoring. Last check p95@3.0s, queue depth trending down. Will post final update after 20m stable window or earlier if status changes. :thumbsup:
